item.text:
<thoughtml>
  <evaluation>
    <program>Tutoring trial</program>
    <comparison>Participating students versus comparison class</comparison>
  </evaluation>
  <findings>
    <academic_improvement>Participating students improved more than the comparison class.</academic_improvement>
    <homework_completion>Teachers observed better homework completion among participating students.</homework_completion>
    <attendance>Attendance gains were small.</attendance>
  </findings>
  <limitations>
    <selection_bias>Participation was voluntary.</selection_bias>
    <baseline_difference>The tutoring group began with more motivated families.</baseline_difference>
    <causal_uncertainty>The observed academic advantage may partly reflect family motivation rather than tutoring alone.</causal_uncertainty>
  </limitations>
  <causal_hypothesis confidence="moderate">
    Tutoring likely improved academic outcomes partly by increasing homework completion, but the current design cannot isolate its effect from pre-existing differences in motivation and family engagement.
  </causal_hypothesis>
  <adoption_decision confidence="moderate">
    Adopt the program as a continued, monitored pilot rather than as conclusively proven intervention.
    Use broader recruitment or random assignment where feasible, measure baseline motivation and prior achievement, and track academic, homework, and attendance outcomes.
  </adoption_decision>
</thoughtml>
